newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Tanker that ran aground in Venezuela refloated.
newsitem.headline: Tanker that ran aground in Venezuela refloated.

text.p: A Maltese-flagged tanker that ran aground Thursday in the outer navigation channel of Lake Maracaibo, in western Venezuela, has been refloated, Maracaibo harbour master said.
The Corelli was able to resume its route to state-oil company company PDVSA's Isla refinery on the Netherlands Antilles island of Curacao, harbour master Adolfo Alvarez told Reuters.
Normal shipping resumed through the channel, the route used for about 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) of Venezuelan crude oil exports, he said.
The Corelli, with a 33,000 tonne cargo of crude, was refloated at 1800 local/2200 GMT. No oil spill resulted.
"As soon as it was refloated, the channel was reopened and boats are transiting normally," Alvarez said.
He said unconfirmed reports that the navigation channel could be closed for dredging appeared premature. A dredge has been operating in the channel for several days, he noted.
The Corelli ran aground at exactly the same spot where two Greek tankers grounded late February and a month ago, with one single-hulled boat spilling at least 28,000 barrels of heavy crude.
